exposure: Birth at or before 26 weeks gestation
cohort: Mothers and newborns in a tertiary care center, comparing mothers who gave birth at or before 26 weeks gestation to the general population
finding: Mothers giving birth at or before 26 weeks gestation experienced more complications and their infants' survival was significantly associated with antenatal steroid use, singleton pregnancy, higher infant admission temperature, and lower CRIB score.
mod_finding: Mothers of infants born at or before 26 weeks gestation had a higher rate of cesarean section compared to the general population.
